page: Amazon Web Services x2idn.16xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features 64 vCPUs and 32 physical cores utilizing the x86_64 architecture with Intel Xeon 8375C processors running at 3.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 1024.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing 16.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, it includes a 1900 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume. The baseline network bandwidth is rated at 50 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the x2idn.16xlarge demonstrates strong multi-core capabilities, achieving a Passmark CPU score of 56725.09 and a multi-core stress-ng CPU performance score of 61925.72. Its memory subsystem delivers a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 3338.18 GB/sec. The instance excels in database operations, scoring 26134.77 on Passmark database tests, and shows strong performance in static web serving throughput at 46.18 GB/sec. It also exhibits strong text generation speeds for small and medium language models, reaching 265.17 tokens/sec on a 135M model and 27.78 tokens/sec on a 7B model.

This instance offers high resource density, particularly in memory capacity and local NVMe storage, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient choice for memory-bound enterprise workloads without requiring external storage overhead. However, single-core performance remains in the average tier, as shown by its Geekbench single-core score of 1688.0, indicating that workloads relying heavily on single-threaded execution may not fully leverage the hardware's premium cost profile. The server is highly suited for memory-intensive databases, large-scale data processing, software compilation, and high-throughput web serving.
